title: Production Planning Rates by Class — Insurance Claim Repairs
content:
Insurance Claim Repairs plans each class's production with three per-class figures: a target key-to-key cycle time, the labor hours a center completes on one vehicle in a business day, and the business days set aside for drop-off, final inspection and delivery.

| Repair class | Target cycle time (business days) | Labor hours per production day | Intake and delivery days (business days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Express Claim Repair | 3 | 6.0 | 1 |
| Standard Claim Repair | 6 | 5.5 | 1 |
| Major Claim Repair | 10 | 5.0 | 1 |
| Structural Claim Repair | 15 | 4.5 | 2 |
| Certified Structural Claim Repair | 18 | 4.0 | 2 |
| Aluminum Certified Structural Claim Repair | 22 | 3.5 | 2 |

### What each column means

1. **Target cycle time** — the target key-to-key cycle time from drop-off to vehicle-ready, in business days. A business day is Monday to Friday, excluding network holidays.
2. **Labor hours per production day** — the labor hours the center completes on one vehicle per business day, stated to one decimal place and used to plan repair days.
3. **Intake and delivery days** — a whole number of business days added to the production days for drop-off, final inspection and delivery when repair days are planned.

### Points of reading

- The figures are fixed by the repair class of the repair order, not by the center or the insurer.
- The intake and delivery allowance doubles from 1 to 2 business days in the three structural classes, while the daily labor figure falls class by class from 6.0 hours in Express Claim Repair to 3.5 hours in Aluminum Certified Structural Claim Repair.
